title: McDonald's Japan says an unauthorized third party accessed its mobile app database
date_note: Both articles (24 November) say the company announced it on Friday, which is 20 November; neither page gives the intrusion date.
geo_basis: country as stated by the sources; no city given
summary: McDonald's Japan said an unauthorized third party accessed the database behind its official mobile app, according to The Record and BleepingComputer. The company says the exposed data include purchase history, IP addresses, customer management IDs and device location data, but not names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses or card information. It is working to invalidate the credentials used and has reported to Japan's data protection authority. No count of affected customers was given.
plain: McDonald's Japan says someone without permission got into the database behind its app. It says purchase history and location data were exposed, but not names, emails, phone numbers, addresses or card details.
exec: A major restaurant chain's app database was accessed; the company says no names or card data were involved and gave no count of affected customers.
action: McDonald's Japan, as The Record reports, says customers did not need to change their passwords or take other security measures.

validation.note: The Record and BleepingComputer, two publishers, each relay McDonald's Japan's statement on the unauthorized access and the data types. McDonald's Japan's own page was not read.
